    Subcategories of the linear quiver and their interval sets #

    A subcategory C of mod Λ_n is determined by the set of intervals [a, d] with M_{a,d} ∈ C (the family 𝕀(C) of Definition 5.4): C consists of the representations all of whose interval summands lie in C (Subcategory.eq_ofIntervals). Consequences:

    • two subcategories containing the same intervals are equal (Subcategory.ext_intervals), and there are finitely many subcategories;
    • the number of isomorphism classes of indecomposables of C is the number of intervals in C (indCard_eq), which identifies |ind C| of the manuscript with the size of 𝕀(C).

    coord (η + θ) i = coord η i + coord θ i

    A retract of a direct sum which is an interval is a retract of one of the summands.

    source
    theorem PretorsionImageClosed.LinearQuiver.eq_of_retract_interval {k : Type u} [Field k] {n : ℕ} {a d a' d' : Fin n} (had : a ≤ d) (had' : a' ≤ d') (h : CategoryTheory.Retract (interval k a' d') (interval k a d)) :
    a' = a ∧ d' = d

    An interval which is a retract of another interval equals it.

      Every representation lies in a subcategory as soon as its interval retracts do; equivalently, a subcategory is determined by its intervals.

      source
